xmldoc.short_description: Read a recording from a delimited text file.

param_input_item.param_description: the delimited text file, one column per lead.
the sampling rate in hertz, required when there is no time column to give it.
the column separator, when it must not be detected from the first line.
the names to assign to the columns.
the unit the file is written in; 'uV' divides the values by a thousand so the recording is in millivolts.
a divisor applied to every value.
true to read the first column as a time even when its header does not announce it.
'seconds' or 'milliseconds', when the time column's unit must not be guessed from the size of its step.
a number of leading lines to drop before the header.
',' for a French export, where the separator is then the semicolon.

param_output_item.param_description: the same kind of struct every reader of the module returns, with info.format set to 'csv'.

description.p: A CSV export is what a spreadsheet or a research rig writes when it has no binary format to reach for, so a reader that refuses it refuses the data most users arrive with.

The delimiter is learnt from the first line: a comma, a semicolon, a tab, or runs of one or more spaces, the last being what a column aligned file uses and a single space would read as empty fields between. A header of names is taken when the first line is not a row of numbers, and its fields become the leads.

A first column that is a monotonic increasing time gives the rate as the median step, which is robust to a dropped sample the way a mean is not, and is then taken off the leads. It is recognised when its header says time, t, seconds or ms, or when the TimeColumn option is true. The step is read as seconds, or as milliseconds when its header says ms, when TimeUnit says so, or when the step is larger than one, because no electrocardiogram is sampled at one hertz. Without a time column the Rate option is required, and the error names it.
The module speaks millivolts, so a file written in microvolts is divided by a thousand, and an explicit scale divides the raw numbers by whatever the rig wrote its samples in.

The file is read whole in one fileread, and the numeric body is parsed with a single sscanf over the whole text rather than with str2double over a split: measured on a 650000 by 2 file on this build, the whole-text scan took about 0.9 second and the split about 2.8 seconds, so the faster one is the one kept, and the whole function reads that file in about 1.1 seconds.

xmldoc.bibliography: Shafranovich, Common Format and MIME Type for Comma-Separated Values (CSV) Files, RFC 4180, 2005.

example_item.example_item_data: % A two lead export at five hundred hertz, the rate given because there is % no time column to carry it. recording = ecglab.readcsv('export.csv', 'Rate', 500); size(recording.samples)

% A French export: the decimal mark is a comma, so the separator is the % semicolon, and the rate comes from a time column in milliseconds. recording = ecglab.readcsv('mesure.csv', 'Decimal', ','); recording.rate
